change.describe: branch `pr-3` of discourse-graphite-3 against e25638dab0d4b98f99c8fe8976ccaae8f4fb9db3 (merge-base e25638d)
change.title: pr-3
change.description: Add BlockedEmail, to block signups based on email. Track stats of how many times each email address is blocked, and last time it was blocked. Move email validation out of User model and into EmailValidator. Signup form remembers which email addresses have failed and shows validation error on email field.
change.author: Neil Lalonde

findings.title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact match, and the unique index on `email` is also case-sensitive. A blocked address such as `Bad@Spam.org` is not matched when the user signs up as `bad@spam.org`, and the reverse also fails. Downcase the email both when saving a BlockedEmail and when looking it up. I did not confirm whether User normalizes the email case before validation.

findings.title: Every email error is added to rejectedEmails and shown as 'invalid'
findings.body: Any `errors.email` entry, such as 'has already been taken', the domain restriction or the blocklist, adds the email to `rejectedEmails`. The client then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message for it, not the server's reason. It also treats the email as rejected for the whole session, even if an admin changes the whitelist, blacklist or blocklist afterwards. Consider showing the server's message.

contracts.action: Server-side email validation now checks the domain whitelist/blacklist and the BlockedEmail table, and the signup failure response now includes errors and values
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed User#email_validator in app/models/user.rb did only the whitelist/blacklist check.
contracts.before_after: The domain check logic is unchanged. A blocklist lookup now runs after it, only when no domain error was added, and it updates match_count and last_match_at.
contracts.visible_effect: The blocked email gets a 'is not allowed.' error. The client adds it to rejectedEmails and marks the field invalid.
contracts.failure_mode: The lookup is case-sensitive, so differently cased variants of a blocked address pass.

summary: The change is functionally sound and `lib/validators` is autoloaded (`config/application.rb:36`). I found three issues: the blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, validation writes to the database and can double-count matches, and every email error is shown on the client as a generic 'invalid'.
